newsitem.title: USA: Witco cutting 1,800 jobs, closing 15 factories.
newsitem.headline: Witco cutting 1,800 jobs, closing 15 factories.

text.p: Witco Corp. said Thursday it would close a third of its factories and eliminate about 1,800 jobs, or a quarter of its work force, over three years as it seeks to become a leading global speciality chemical company.

The company added that it will take a pre-tax charge of $421 million in the fourth quarter for the costs of the restructuring and for other items, including environmental and safety compliance, litigation provisions and inventory writedowns.
Witco, based in Greenwich, Conn., said the restructuring is intended to reduce annual operating costs by more than $200 million by the end of 1999.
The plan anticipates a reduction in the company's worldwide manufacturing facilities from 46 to 31, as well as consolidation of certain related distribution and administrative centres.
As a result, Witco said, it will lay off 1,800 of its current 6,800 employees, or about 26 percent of the work force.
Witco also said it will invest more than $600 million over the next three years to modernise remaining manufacturing facilities, add new capacity and upgrade its worldwide information systems.
"Our goal is nothing less than becoming the preeminent speciality chemical company in the world," Chairman E. Gary Cook said in a statement.
"The restructuring is necessary to achieve the efficient, productive, competitive and agile company necessary to meet the ever more demanding needs of our global customers.
"We regret the hardship this places on many of our employees, but we have established programmes to ease the transition for those impacted."

The company said the plan was designed to achieve previously stated goals of a 20 percent reduction in fixed costs, a reduction of between 5 percent and 10 percent in variable costs and a net working capital reduction of 25 percent.
Witco's stock added $1.875 to $32.50 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
